import subprocess
import threading


def worker(cmd):
    subprocess.run(cmd)


argv = ["pacman", "-S", "r22-thread-run"]
t = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(argv,))
t.run()
rationale: Python 3.14 semantics: Thread.__init__ binds self._target=worker, self._args=(argv,), self._kwargs={} at construction (threading.py:925-928). t.run() is a plain method call on the stored object; Thread.run invokes self._target(*self._args, **self._kwargs) synchronously in the calling thread (threading.py:1023-1024), with no start() and no new thread. argv is a module-scope literal list bound before construction and never rebound, so worker executes subprocess.run(["pacman","-S","r22-thread-run"]) with a fully determined argv. Serialized with shlex.join: 'pacman -S r22-thread-run'. A scanner that follows calls to statically known callables therefore owes exactly one observed host_mutation row and zero unparsed counters. The r21 F4 miss (only .start on a scheduled binding was followed; .run fell through to unresolved and emitted nothing) must not recur; silent absence fails this exact expectation.
